# Functions

To reduce code, we will generate some functions here. 

```{r definition, echo = F}
# function to generate a vulcano plot for differentially expressed genes
GenerateVolcanoPlot <- function(fit, variable, file) {
  # get all hits
  hits <- topTable(fit, coef = variable, number = Inf, adjust.method = "BH")
  total <- nrow(hits)
  # get first hit after FDR 10% for drawing a p-value threshold line
  index <- if(length(which(hits$adj.P.Val < 0.1)) == 0) 0 else which(hits$adj.P.Val < 0.1)
  threshold <- hits[index[length(index)] + 1, "P.Value"]
  ### volcano plot ###
  # label only significant hits (if more than 10)
  g <- ggplot(hits, aes(x = logFC, y = -log10(P.Value))) + 
    theme_bw(base_size = 22) + 
    geom_point() + 
    xlim(-2, 2) + 
    ylim(0, 6) +
    xlab(bquote(~Log[2]~ "fold change")) +
    ylab(bquote(~-Log[10]~ italic(P))) +
    theme(axis.line = element_line(),
      panel.border = element_blank(),
      panel.background = element_blank()) +
    labs(caption = paste0("Total variables: ", total)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(threshold), linetype = "dashed")
 if(length(index) >= 10){
    g + geom_point(data = hits[index, ], aes(x = LogFC, y = -log10(P.Value)), colour = "red2", size = 2) +
    geom_text_repel(data = hits[index[1:10], ], aes(label = gene_name), colour = "red2")
  # else: label hit genes (if some are found) purple and following genes green until a maximum of 10 genes is labeled
  } else if(length(index) == 0) {
    g + geom_text_repel(data = hits[1:10, ], aes(label = gene_name))
  } else {
    g + geom_point(data = hits[index, ], aes(x = LogFC, y = -log10(P.Value)), colour = "red2", size = 2) +
    geom_text_repel(data = hits[index, ], aes(label = gene_name), colour = "red2") +
    geom_point(data = hits[(length(index) + 1):10, ], aes(x = LogFC, y = -log10(P.Value)), size = 2) +
    geom_text_repel(data = hits[(length(index) + 1):10, ], aes(label = gene_name))
  }
  ggsave(plot = g, file = paste0(outpath, "/", file), width = 8, height = 6, units = "in")
}

# function to plot all differentially expressed hits for the different covariates corrected for all other covariates as a vertical barplot
GenerateVerticalBarplotOfDiffExprHits <- function(design, fit, from, to, plot_name){
  # Get padj values for all different covariates
  nc <- ncol(design) - 1
  limma_res_fc <- topTable(fit, adjust = "BH", sort.by = "none", number = Inf)
  limma_res_padj <- limma_res_fc[, from:(to + nc)]
  for (i in 1:nc){
    limma_res_padj[, i] = topTable(fit, adjust = "BH", sort.by = "none", number = Inf, coef = i + 1)[, "adj.P.Val"]
    if(i == nc){
      limma_res_padj$`Ensembl Gene ID` = topTable(fit, adjust = "BH", sort.by = "none", number = Inf, coef = i + 1)[, "gene_id"]
    }
  }
  limma_res_padj <- limma_res_padj[, -c(length(limma_res_padj) - 1)] # remove SV1
  colnames(limma_res_padj) <- c("Diagnosis", "Age", "Sex", "pH", "PMI", "RIN", "RIN2", "Suicide", "Type_of_Death1", "Type_of_Death2", "C1", "C2", "C3", "C4", "Ensembl Gene ID")
  limma_res_padj$Type_of_Death <- (limma_res_padj$Type_of_Death1 + limma_res_padj$Type_of_Death2) / 2
  limma_res_padj <- limma_res_padj[, c("Diagnosis", "Age", "Sex", "pH", "PMI", "RIN", "RIN2", "Suicide", "Type_of_Death", "C1", "C2", "C3", "C4", "Ensembl Gene ID")]
  # unmerge Gene Ensembl IDs at their vertical dash "|"
  limma_res_padj <- unique(separate_rows(limma_res_padj, `Ensembl Gene ID`, sep = "\\|")) 
  # change data.frame into data.table to get the minimal adjusted p-value for each unique Ensembl Gene IDs (some can be found multipe times!!)
  limma_res_padj <- as.data.table(limma_res_padj)
  limma_res_padj <- limma_res_padj[, lapply(.SD, min), by = 'Ensembl Gene ID']
  # check, how many padj values are < 0.10
  limma_res_padj_0.1 <- apply(limma_res_padj[, -1], 2, function(x) sum(x < 0.1))
  limma_res_plot <- data.frame(sort(limma_res_padj_0.1, decreasing = T))
  # vertical barplot with ggplot2
  g <- ggplot(limma_res_plot, aes(y = sort.limma_res_padj_0.1..decreasing...T., x = reorder(row.names(limma_res_plot), sort.limma_res_padj_0.1..decreasing...T.))) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
    coord_flip() +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(text = element_text(size = 22)) +
    ylab("# significant hits") +
    xlab("") +
    geom_text(size = 7, aes(label = sort.limma_res_padj_0.1..decreasing...T.), nudge_y = 120, colour = "dimgray") + 
    scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0.02, 0.01))
  ggsave(plot = g, file = paste0(outpath, "/", plot_name))
  return(limma_res_plot)
}

# function, which first generates the contingency table for two datasets and then calculates the p-value using fisher exact test
# return: the p-value calculated using fisher exact test
FishersExactTest <- function(data1, data2, background){
  data1  <- unique(sort(unlist(data1)))
  data2 <- intersect(data2, background)  # take only the genes, which are also in the background data
  a <- length(intersect(data1, data2))  # all genes in data1 and data2
  b <- length(data1) - a  # all genes in data1, but NOT in data2
  x <- length(setdiff(data2, data1))  # all genes in data2, but NOT data1
  y <- length(background) - length(data1) - x  # all genes NOT in data1 or data2
  contingency_matrix <- matrix(c(a, x, b, y), 2, 2)
  #print(contingency_matrix)
  result <- fisher.test(contingency_matrix, alternative = "greater")
  return(result$p.value)
}

# function to generate a forest plot for a given gene: showing a horizontal line from lower to upper 95% confidence interval and a dot in the middle representing the mean log2FC for the gene, its transcripts and exons. The FDR will only be plotted for the gene for the normal model and one transcript and one exon based on the new FDR model.
GenerateForestPlot <- function(gene) {
  # we will save following order of IDs for the plot: 1. Gene ID, 2. Transcript ID and 3. Exon ID with increasing character length, so that merged IDs are coming last
  id_order <- vector() 
  # 1. load DEA gene results, save only necessary information for the gene of interest, change column names and save order of IDs
  load(paste0(results_path, "/1.1_diff_expr_genes_for_diagnosis.RData"))
  gene_expr <- top_hits[top_hits$`Gene Symbol` == gene, ][, c("Ensembl Gene ID", "LogFC", "95% Confidence Interval, lower bound", "95% Confidence Interval, upper bound", "FDR estimate")]
  colnames(gene_expr) <- c("ID", "LogFC", "CI_lower", "CI_upper", "FDR")
  id_order <- c(id_order, gene_expr[order(nchar(gene_expr$ID)), ]$ID)
  # 2. load DEA transcript results (for normal model, including all transcripts) and perform same steps as above
  load(paste0(results_path, "/2.1_diff_expr_transcripts_for_diagnosis.RData"))
  transcript_expr <- top_hits[top_hits$`Gene Symbol` == gene, ][, c("Ensembl Transcript ID", "LogFC", "95% Confidence Interval, lower bound", "95% Confidence Interval, upper bound", "FDR estimate")]
  # change all FDRs to 1 (as we only want to keep the ones with the new FDRs)
  transcript_expr$`FDR estimate` <- 1
  colnames(transcript_expr) <- c("ID", "LogFC", "CI_lower", "CI_upper", "FDR")
  id_order <- c(id_order, transcript_expr[order(nchar(transcript_expr$ID)), ]$ID)
  # 3. load DEA exon results (same steps as for transcripts above)
  load(paste0(results_path, "/3.1_diff_expr_exons_for_diagnosis.RData"))
  exon_expr <- top_hits[top_hits$`Gene Symbol` == gene, ][, c("Ensembl Exon ID", "LogFC", "95% Confidence Interval, lower bound", "95% Confidence Interval, upper bound", "FDR estimate")]
  exon_expr$`FDR estimate` <- 1
  colnames(exon_expr) <- c("ID", "LogFC", "CI_lower", "CI_upper", "FDR")
  id_order <- c(id_order, exon_expr[order(nchar(exon_expr$ID)), ]$ID)
  # merge all three datasets using rbind
  all <- rbind(gene_expr, transcript_expr, exon_expr)
  # change ID column to factor and refactor using the saved order
  all$ID <- as.factor(all$ID)
  all$ID <- factor(all$ID, levels = rev(id_order))
  
  # get number of filtered/total transcripts and exons
  filtered_transcripts <- length(unique(separate_rows(transcript_expr, "ID", sep = "\\|")$ID))
  total_transcripts <- length(unique(gencode[gencode$gene_name == gene & gencode$type == "transcript", ]$transcript_id))
  filtered_exons <- length(unique(separate_rows(exon_expr, "ID", sep = "\\|")$ID))
  total_exons <- length(unique(gencode[gencode$gene_name == gene & gencode$type == "exon", ]$exon_id))
  
  # update the "two" FDRs (one transcript, one exon):
  # load DEA transcript results for new p-value/FDR correction
  load(paste0(results_path, "/2.4_diff_expr_transcripts_for_diagnosis_new_pvalue_and_fdr.RData"))
  transcript_expr <- top_hits[top_hits$`Gene Symbol` == gene, ][, c("Ensembl Transcript ID", "FDR estimate")]
  # change FDR for the given transcript ID in the merged dataset
  all[all$ID == transcript_expr$`Ensembl Transcript ID`, "FDR"] <- transcript_expr$`FDR estimate`
  # load DEA exon results for new p-value/FDR correction
  load(paste0(results_path, "/3.4_diff_expr_exons_for_diagnosis_new_pvalue_and_fdr.RData"))
  exon_expr <- top_hits[top_hits$`Gene Symbol` == gene, ][, c("Ensembl Exon ID", "FDR estimate")]
  # change FDR for the given exon ID in the merged dataset
  all[all$ID == exon_expr$`Ensembl Exon ID`, "FDR"] <- exon_expr$`FDR estimate`

  # generate Plot
  g <- ggplot(all, aes(x = ID, y = LogFC, ymin = CI_lower, ymax = CI_upper))+
  geom_pointrange() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  geom_text(label = ifelse(all$FDR < 1, paste0("FDR = ", round(all$FDR, 2)), ""), aes(hjust = -0.5, vjust = -0.2)) +
  coord_flip() +
  ggtitle(paste0(gene_expr$ID, " (", gene, ")\n# filtered transcripts: ", (total_transcripts - filtered_transcripts), "; # total transcripts: ", total_transcripts, "\n# filtered exons: ", (total_exons - filtered_exons), "; # total exons: ", total_exons)) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) +
  xlab("") +
  ylab(bquote("Log"["2"]*"(Fold Change)"))
  # save plot
  ggsave(plot = g, file = paste0(outpath, "/4_forest_plot_for_gene_", gene, ".pdf"), width = 12.5, height = 5.75)
  g
}
```

## GENCODE

And GENCODE to get the original number of genes, transcripts and exons. We will filter it exactly as in the preprocessing step (only protein-coding genes from the HAVANA source).
```{r}
gencode <- import.gff("/storage/groups/ccm01/datasets/2018_MPIP-Dean_postmortem_brain/annotation_files/gencode.v19.annotation.gtf", format = "gtf")
gencode <- gencode[gencode$gene_type == "protein_coding"]
```

### Boxplot

For the TRIM10 hit, we will plot the residuals of sex vs. diagnosis as this gene infers a difference between these two covariates. To generate the TRIM10 boxplot we will use the results from the normal model to see the difference between the two sexes.
```{r, echo = F}
# load data
load(paste0(results_path, "/1.1_diff_expr_genes_for_diagnosis.RData"))
# generate boxplot with case vs control for male and female samples of the hit gene (TRIM10)
trim10 <- res[rownames(res) == "ENSG00000204613.6", ]
trim10 <- t(t(as.data.frame(trim10)))
trim10 <- merge(trim10, pData(gene_summaries)[, c("ShortName", "Dx", "Sex")], by.x = "row.names", by.y = "ShortName", all.x = T)
trim10$DxSex <- paste0(trim10$Dx, trim10$Sex)
g <- ggplot(trim10, aes(Sex, trim10, fill = Dx)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("Female", "Male")) +
  theme_classic() + 
  theme(text = element_text(size = 22), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = viridis(3), labels = c("Controls", "Cases")) + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) + 
  ggtitle("TRIM10") +
  ylab("Gene expression") + 
  xlab("Sex") + 
  labs(fill = "Diagnosis")
ggsave(plot = g, file = paste0(outpath, "/1.2_boxplot_TRIM10_diff_expr_genes_for_diagnosis_with_sex_dx_interaction.pdf"), width = 7, height = 6)
g
# p-value females
females <- trim10[trim10$Sex == "F",]
case <- females[females$Dx == "CASE",]
control <- females[females$Dx == "CTL",]
t.test(case$trim10, control$trim10) # p-value = 0.01022
# p-value males
males <- trim10[trim10$Sex == "M",]
case <- males[males$Dx == "CASE",]
control <- males[males$Dx == "CTL",]
t.test(case$trim10, control$trim10) # p-value = 0.05302
# remove unnecessary data
rm(design, fit, res, trim10, females, males, case, control, g)
```

## New FDR model

As we have a lot of transcripts (N = 100,750), we are not getting any hits as the FDR correction overcorrects. Therefore, we picked for each gene the transcript with the lowest p-value and rerun the DEA (FDR calculation) only for the gene based transcripts, resulting in tDEGene hits. This procedure we call here: new FDR model.

### Load data

Load the tDEGene dataset.
```{r}
# load RData file
load(paste0(results_path, "/2.4_diff_expr_transcripts_for_diagnosis_new_pvalue_and_fdr.RData"))
```

### Volcano plot 

Generate a volcano plot.
```{r}
# volcano plot
GenerateVolcanoPlot(fit, variable = "DxCASE", file = "2.4_volcano_plot_diff_expr_transcripts_for_diagnosis_new_pvalue_and_fdr.pdf")
```

### Barplot of tDEGenes (all covariates)

Get tDEGenes for each covariate (corrected for all the other covariates).
```{r, echo = F}
# generate vertical barplot
limma_res_transcript.new <- GenerateVerticalBarplotOfDiffExprHits(design, fit, from = 5, to = 4, plot_name = "2.4_barplot_significant_DEA_hits_transcripts_new_pvalue_and_fdr.pdf")
ggplot(limma_res_transcript.new, aes(y = sort.limma_res_padj_0.1..decreasing...T., x = reorder(row.names(limma_res_transcript.new), sort.limma_res_padj_0.1..decreasing...T.))) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
    coord_flip() +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(text = element_text(size = 22)) +
    ylab("# significant hits") +
    xlab("") +
    geom_text(size = 7, aes(label = sort.limma_res_padj_0.1..decreasing...T.), nudge_y = 120, colour = "dimgray") + 
    scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0.02, 0.01))
```

### Heatmap of tDEGenes (diagnosis)

Now, we generate some plots for the six found tDEGenes for diagnosis. First, we will plot a heatmap of the six tDEGenes.
```{r, echo = F}
# get only top hits (6 tDEGenes)
top_hits <- top_hits[top_hits$`FDR estimate` < 0.1, ]
# ǵenerate heatmap of hits
anno <- pData(transcript_summaries)[, c("Age", "PMI", "RIN", "Sex", "Suicide", "Dx", "ShortName")]
rownames(anno) <- anno$ShortName
anno$ShortName <- NULL
pheatmap(exprs(transcript_summaries)[top_hits$`Ensembl Transcript ID`, ], scale = "row", annotation_col = anno, show_colnames = F)
pheatmap(exprs(transcript_summaries)[top_hits$`Ensembl Transcript ID`, ], scale = "row", annotation_col = anno, show_colnames = F, filename = paste0(outpath, "/2.4_heatmap_significant_DEA_hits_transcripts_new_pvalue_and_fdr.pdf"))
dev.off()
```

### Barplot of up/down-regulated tDEGenes (diagnosis)

Then, we plot the up and down regulated genes into one barplot with the two variables mirrored on the x-axis.
```{r, echo = F}
logfc <- as.data.frame(table(top_hits$LogFC))
logfc$group <- "Upregulated"
logfc[as.numeric(as.character(logfc$Var1)) < 0, "group"] <- "Downregulated"
logfc[as.numeric(as.character(logfc$Var1)) < 0, "Freq"] <- -1
logfc$Var1 <- abs(round(as.numeric(as.character(logfc$Var1)), 2))
logfc$logfc <- 2^logfc$Var1
logfc$linearFC <- sapply(logfc$logfc, function(x) {if(as.double(as.character(x)) >= 1 || is.na(x)){x} else {-1/x}})
# generate barplot
g <- ggplot(logfc, aes(x = linearFC, y = Freq, fill = group)) + 
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "identity", show.legend = F, orientation = logfc$Freq) + 
  xlab("linear fold change") +
  ylab("# tDEGenes (FDR < 10%)") +
  xlim(1, 1.5) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(axis.line.x.bottom = element_line(colour = "black"), axis.line.y.left = element_line(colour = "black"), axis.ticks.length = unit(.15, "cm"), axis.ticks = element_line(colour = "black")) + 
  annotate("text", x = 1.4, y = 1.3, label = paste0("No. of genes upregulated: ", length(logfc[logfc$group == "Upregulated", "group"])), size = 4) +
  annotate("text", x = 1.4, y = -1.3, label = paste0("No. of genes downregulated: ", length(logfc[logfc$group == "Downregulated", "group"])), size = 4) + 
  scale_fill_viridis(discrete = T, end = 0.8)
ggsave(plot = g, file = paste0(outpath, "/2.4_barplot_up_down_regulated_significant_DEA_hits_transcripts_new_pvalue_and_fdr.pdf"), width = 5.43, height = 3.45, units = "in")
g
rm(logfc, g)
```

### Violin plots of tDEGenes (diagnosis)


## PRS with new FDR model

We will generate a barplot of the number of hits, we get using the different calculated polygenic risk scores. 

### Load datasets

We need to load all PRS transcript DEA hits and save only the number of found hits (FDR < 10% and FDR < 5%) into a table.
```{r}
prs_all <- c("ADHD-2017", "ASD-2019", "BIP-2018", "BMI-2015", "CDG1-2013", "CDG2-2018", "EA-2018", "HE-2014", "IN-2018", "MDD1-2012", "MDD2-2018", "MDD3-2019", "SCZ2-2014")
prs_transcripts <- data.frame("PRS" = character(), "FDR_0.1" = numeric(), "FDR_0.05" = numeric())
count = 1
for (p in prs_all) {
  prs <- fread(paste0(results_path, "/2.5.", count, "_diff_expr_transcripts_for_", p, "_PRS_new_pvalue_and_fdr.csv"), select = c("Gene Symbol", "FDR estimate"), stringsAsFactors = F)
  fdr10 <- length(unique(prs[prs$`FDR estimate` < 0.10, ]$`Gene Symbol`))
  fdr5 <- length(unique(prs[prs$`FDR estimate` < 0.05, ]$`Gene Symbol`))
  new_row <- data.frame("PRS" = p, "FDR_0.1" = fdr10, "FDR_0.05" = fdr5)
  prs_transcripts <- rbind(prs_transcripts, new_row)
  count = count + 1
}
```

Now, we can generate a barplot for all the PRS based DEA hits on transcript level, also called transcript expression quantitative trait score (teQTS).

```{r, echo = F}
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 1, vjust = 1)) +

  scale_fill_manual(values = viridis(2, begin = 0.3, end = 0.9, option = "D"), labels = c("FDR < 0.01", "FDR < 0.05")) +
  geom_text(label = plot_prs$value)
ggsave(plot = g, file = paste0(outpath, "/2.5_barplot_ALL_PRS_diff_expr_transcripts_for_PRS_new_pvalue_and_fdr.pdf"))
g
```

## PRS with new FDR model

We will generate a barplot of the number of hits, we get using the different calculated polygenic risk scores. And we will combine the PRS DEGenes based on transcript and exon level with FDR < 10% in one plot. 

### Load datasets

We need to load all PRS exon DEA hits and save only the number of found hits (FDR < 10% and FDR < 5%) into a table.
```{r}
prs_all <- c("ADHD-2017", "ASD-2019", "BIP-2018", "BMI-2015", "CDG1-2013", "CDG2-2018", "EA-2018", "HE-2014", "IN-2018", "MDD1-2012", "MDD2-2018", "MDD3-2019", "SCZ2-2014")
prs_exons <- data.frame("PRS" = character(), "FDR_0.1" = numeric(), "FDR_0.05" = numeric())
count = 1
for (p in prs_all) {
  prs <- fread(paste0(results_path, "/3.5.", count, "_diff_expr_exons_for_", p, "_PRS_new_pvalue_and_fdr.csv"), select = c("Gene Symbol", "FDR estimate"), stringsAsFactors = F)
  fdr10 <- length(unique(prs[prs$`FDR estimate` < 0.10, ]$`Gene Symbol`))
  fdr5 <- length(unique(prs[prs$`FDR estimate` < 0.05, ]$`Gene Symbol`))
  new_row <- data.frame("PRS" = p, "FDR_0.1" = fdr10, "FDR_0.05" = fdr5)
  prs_exons <- rbind(prs_exons, new_row)
  count = count + 1
}
```

Now, we combine Transcript and Exon hits for FDR < 10% in one plot:

# Age DEGenes

## Load data

First, we need to load the gene-based (gDEGenes), transcript-based (tDEGenes) and exon-based (eDEGenes) differentially expressed genes for age. Then, we filter the data for only significant (FDR < 10%) genes. 
```{r}
# gene-level
gDEGenes_age <- fread(paste0(results_path, "/1.1_diff_expr_genes_for_age.csv"), select = c("Ensembl Gene ID", "Gene Symbol", "FDR estimate"), data.table = F)
bck_gDEGenes_age <- unique(sort(gDEGenes_age$`Ensembl Gene ID`))
gDEGenes_age <- gDEGenes_age[gDEGenes_age$`FDR estimate` < 0.1, ]

# transcript-level
tDEGenes_age <- fread(paste0(results_path, "/2.4_diff_expr_transcripts_for_age_new_pvalue_and_fdr.csv"), select = c("FDR estimate", "Gene Symbol", "Ensembl Gene ID"), data.table = F)
bck_tDEGenes_age <- unique(sort(tDEGenes_age$`Ensembl Gene ID`))
tDEGenes_age <- tDEGenes_age[tDEGenes_age$`FDR estimate` < 0.1, ]

# exon-level
eDEGenes_age <- fread(paste0(results_path, "/3.4_diff_expr_exons_for_age_new_pvalue_and_fdr.csv"), select = c("FDR estimate", "Gene Symbol", "Ensembl Gene ID"), data.table = F)
bck_eDEGenes_age <- unique(sort(eDEGenes_age$`Ensembl Gene ID`))
eDEGenes_age <- eDEGenes_age[eDEGenes_age$`FDR estimate` < 0.1, ]
```

## Overlap to known ageing genes

Now, we are interested in how many of the differentially expressed age genes are overlapping to a database of known ageing genes for human. Therefore, we use the ageing gene database called GenAge and download all human age related genes from their website: https://genomics.senescence.info/download.html

First, we load the known ageing genes from the GenAge database. 
```{r}
ageing_genes <- fread("/storage/groups/ccm01/datasets/2019_Human_Ageing_Genomic_Resources/genage_human.csv", select = "symbol", data.table = F)
```

Then, we calculate the overlap to the single age DEGenes from our dataset:
```{r}
# gDEGenes
print(paste0("Age gDEGenes overlap to known age genes: ", length(intersect(ageing_genes$symbol, gDEGenes_age$`Gene Symbol`))))

# tDEGenes
print(paste0("Age tDEGenes overlap to known age genes: ", length(intersect(ageing_genes$symbol, tDEGenes_age$`Gene Symbol`))))

# eDEGenes
print(paste0("Age eDEGenes overlap to known age genes: ", length(intersect(ageing_genes$symbol, eDEGenes_age$`Gene Symbol`))))
```

Now, we can also check the significance (p-value) of the overlap from our age DEGenes to the known age genes. Therefore, we first need to generate a contingency table and then run Fisher's exact test:

1. gDEGenes: `r FishersExactTest(gDEGenes_age[, "Gene Symbol"], ageing_genes$symbol, bck_gDEGenes_age)`
2. tDEGenes: `r FishersExactTest(tDEGenes_age[, "Gene Symbol"], ageing_genes$symbol, bck_tDEGenes_age)`
3. eDEGenes: `r FishersExactTest(eDEGenes_age[, "Gene Symbol"], ageing_genes$symbol, bck_eDEGenes_age)`

## VENN diagram

When, we will generate a VENN diagram for the overlap of found eDEGenes, tDEGenes and eDEGenes for age and save it into a pdf file.  

# FUMA

## Load data

```{r}
# FUMA tDEGene results
tDEGenes_fuma <- fread(paste0(fuma_path, "/Trans/FUMA_gene2func31297/gtex_v8_ts_DEG.txt"), select = c("Category", "GeneSet", "p", "adjP"))
tDEGenes_fuma$log_adjP <- -log10(tDEGenes_fuma$adjP)

# FUMA eDEGene results
eDEGenes_fuma <- fread(paste0(fuma_path,"/Exon/FUMA_gene2func31296/gtex_v8_ts_DEG.txt"), select = c("Category", "GeneSet", "p", "adjP"))
eDEGenes_fuma <- eDEGenes_fuma[eDEGenes_fuma$adjP < 0.05, ]
eDEGenes_fuma$log_adjP <- -log10(eDEGenes_fuma$adjP)
eDEGenes_fuma <- eDEGenes_fuma[eDEGenes_fuma$Category == "DEG.twoside", ]
eDEGenes_fuma <- eDEGenes_fuma[order(eDEGenes_fuma$GeneSet, decreasing = T), ]

# merge tDEGenes and eDEGenes
tDEGenes_fuma <- tDEGenes_fuma[tDEGenes_fuma$GeneSet %in% eDEGenes_fuma$GeneSet, ]
tDEGenes_fuma$type <- "tDEGenes"
eDEGenes_fuma$type <- "eDEGenes"
fuma <- rbind(tDEGenes_fuma, eDEGenes_fuma)
```

# Gene set (Pathway) enrichment analysis

## Load data

First, we will read in the tDEGenes and eDEGenes for diagnosis. 
```{r}
# tDEGenes 
tDEGenes <- fread(paste0(results_path, "/2.4_diff_expr_transcripts_for_diagnosis_new_pvalue_and_fdr.csv"), sep = "\t", select = c("Ensembl Transcript ID", "Gene Symbol", "FDR estimate"), stringsAsFactors = F)
tDEGenes <- tDEGenes[tDEGenes$`FDR estimate` < 0.1, c("Ensembl Transcript ID", "Gene Symbol")]

# eDEGenes
eDEGenes <- fread(paste0(results_path, "/3.4_diff_expr_exons_for_diagnosis_new_pvalue_and_fdr.csv"), sep = "\t", select = c("Ensembl Exon ID", "Gene Symbol", "FDR estimate"), stringsAsFactors = F)

# save background gene number (all given genes from the dataset)
background_genes <- as.data.frame(eDEGenes[!is.na(eDEGenes$`Gene Symbol`) & eDEGenes$`Gene Symbol` != "", ])[, "Gene Symbol"]

# get only significant hits
eDEGenes <- eDEGenes[eDEGenes$`FDR estimate` < 0.1, c("Ensembl Exon ID", "Gene Symbol")]
```

## VENN overlap

Before, we perform the GSEA, we will generate a VENN diagram of the overlap of the tDEGenes and eDEGenes. As all six tDEGenes are also eDEGene hits, the VENN diagram should display a huge circle (2,224 eDEGenes) with a smaller circle (6 tDEGenes) inside. 
```{r, echo = F}
# show plot 
grid.newpage()
draw.pairwise.venn(area1 = length(unique(tDEGenes$`Gene Symbol`)), 
                   area2 = length(unique(eDEGenes$`Gene Symbol`)), 
                   cross.area = length(intersect(unique(tDEGenes$`Gene Symbol`),
                                                 unique(eDEGenes$`Gene Symbol`))), 
                   fill = c(rgb(red = 66, green = 146, blue = 198, maxColorValue = 255),
                            rgb(red = 158, green = 212, blue = 0, maxColorValue = 255)),
                   category = c(paste("tDEGenes", length(unique(tDEGenes$`Gene Symbol`)),
                                      sep = "\n"), 
                                paste("eDEGenes", length(unique(eDEGenes$`Gene Symbol`)),
                                      sep = "\n")), lty = "blank", cex = 2)
dev.off()
# save plot
pdf(paste0(outpath, "/4_VENN_tDEGenes_eDEGenes_overlap.pdf"))
grid.newpage()
draw.pairwise.venn(area1 = length(unique(tDEGenes$`Gene Symbol`)), 
                   area2 = length(unique(eDEGenes$`Gene Symbol`)), 
                   cross.area = length(intersect(unique(tDEGenes$`Gene Symbol`),
                                                 unique(eDEGenes$`Gene Symbol`))), 
                   fill = c(rgb(red = 66, green = 146, blue = 198, maxColorValue = 255),
                            rgb(red = 158, green = 212, blue = 0, maxColorValue = 255)),
                   category = c(paste("tDEGenes", length(unique(tDEGenes$`Gene Symbol`)),
                                      sep = "\n"), 
                                paste("eDEGenes", length(unique(eDEGenes$`Gene Symbol`)),
                                      sep = "\n")), lty = "blank", cex = 2)
dev.off()
```

## Load MSigDB

For the gene set enrichment, sometimes also called pathway enrichment, we will use the sub-collection of "Canonical pathways" from the "C2: curated gene sets" and the "c5: gene ontology (GO) gene sets" of the Molecular Signature DataBase (MSigDB) downloaded from the GSEA website: http://software.broadinstitute.org/gsea/downloads.jsp

We load the data as Gene Set Collections (multiple Gene Sets), where the gene set (pathway) name is the key and all included genes (symbols) of the gene set are stored in a list (value). It is similar to a dictionary in python or a hashmap in Java with a key (gene set name) and value (list of included genes) pair.
```{r}
# load MSigDB c2 - canonical pathways
all_canonical <- getGmt("/storage/groups/ccm01/datasets/2020_MSigDB_v7.0/c2.cp.v7.0.symbols.gmt", 
                  collectionType = BroadCollection(category = "c2"),  
                  geneIdType = SymbolIdentifier())
# load MSigDB c5 - gene ontology (GO) 
all_go <- getGmt("/storage/groups/ccm01/datasets/2020_MSigDB_v7.0/c5.all.v7.0.symbols.gmt", 
                  collectionType = BroadCollection(category = "c5"),  
                  geneIdType = SymbolIdentifier())
```
<!-- **TODO:** As the gene symbols are not as sufficient as Ensembl Gene IDs, we will map the gene symbols to Ensembl IDs using the latest GENCODE file created on GRCh37 (hg19) release 19 (downloaded from: https://www.gencodegenes.org/human/release_19.html). --> 


## Gene set (Pathway) enrichment analysis

Now, we use the MGSA tool to find pathways which are enriched for our dataset. As we only have six hits on transcript level (6 tDEGenes), it does not make sense to run a pathway/gene set enrichment on these as no pathway will be enriched with such a low number of genes. So, we will do the enrichment analysis only on the 2223 eDEGene hits. 

### MSigDB - Canonical Pathways

```{r}
cp_mgsa <- list()
for (gset in all_canonical) {
  t <- list(gset@geneIds)
 cp_mgsa <- c(cp_mgsa, t)
}
names(cp_mgsa) <- names(all_canonical)
set.seed(0)  # necessary to get the same results all the time!!
cp_res <- mgsa(o = as.character(unique(eDEGenes$`Gene Symbol`)[!is.na(unique(eDEGenes$`Gene Symbol`))]), sets = cp_mgsa, population = as.character(background_genes))
plot(cp_res)
dev.off()

mgsa_res_cp <- setsResults(cp_res)
head(mgsa_res_cp[order(mgsa_res_cp$estimate, decreasing = T),])
write.table(mgsa_res_cp, file = paste0(results_path, "/3.6_GSEA_MGSA_MSigDB_c2_canonical_pathways_results_eDEGenes.tsv"))
```

Generate a barplot for the top (significant: estimate > 0.5) pathway hits.  
```{r, echo = F}
# save only the significant pathways (score > 0.5)
mgsa_res_cp <- mgsa_res_cp[mgsa_res_cp$estimate > 0.5 & !is.na(mgsa_res_cp$estimate), ]
mgsa_res_cp <- mgsa_res_cp[!(row.names(mgsa_res_cp) == "NA"), ]
plot_mgsa_cp <- as.data.frame(mgsa_res_cp[order(mgsa_res_cp$estimate, decreasing = T), ])
## set the levels in order we want
g <- ggplot(data = plot_mgsa_cp, aes(x = reorder(row.names(plot_mgsa_cp), estimate), y = estimate)) + geom_bar(stat = "identity") + xlab("") + coord_flip() + theme_minimal() + ggtitle("MsigDB: c2 - cp") + geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "red")
ggsave(plot = g, file = paste0(outpath, "/3.6_barplot_eDEGenes_MSigDB_top10_enriched_c2_canonical_pathways.pdf"), width = 5, height = 2)
g
```

### MSigDB - GO gene sets

```{r}
go_mgsa <- list()
for (gset in all_go) {
  t <- list(gset@geneIds)
 go_mgsa <- c(go_mgsa, t)
}
names(go_mgsa) <- names(all_go)
set.seed(0)  # necessary to get the same results all the time!!
go_res <- mgsa(o = as.character(unique(eDEGenes$`Gene Symbol`)[!is.na(unique(eDEGenes$`Gene Symbol`))]), sets = go_mgsa, population = as.character(background_genes))
plot(go_res)

mgsa_res_go <- setsResults(go_res)
head(mgsa_res_go[order(mgsa_res_go$estimate, decreasing = T), ])
write.table(mgsa_res_go, file = paste0(results_path, "/3.6_GSEA_MGSA_MSigDB_c5_all_GO_gene_sets_results_eDEGenes.tsv"))
```

Generate a barplot for the top (significant: estimate > 0.5) pathway hits.  
```{r, echo = F}
# save only significant (estimate > 0.5) pathways
mgsa_res_go <- mgsa_res_go[mgsa_res_go$estimate > 0.5 & !is.na(mgsa_res_go$estimate), ]
mgsa_res_go <- mgsa_res_go[!(row.names(mgsa_res_go) == "NA"), ]
plot_mgsa_go <- as.data.frame(mgsa_res_go[order(mgsa_res_go$estimate, decreasing = T), ])
## set the levels in order we want
g <- ggplot(data = plot_mgsa_go, aes(x = reorder(row.names(plot_mgsa_go), estimate), y = estimate)) + geom_bar(stat = "identity") + xlab("") + coord_flip() + theme_minimal() + ggtitle("MsigDB: c5 - GO") + geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "red")
ggsave(plot = g, file = paste0(outpath, "/3.6_barplot_eDEGenes_MSigDB_top10_enriched_c5_all_GO_gene_sets.pdf"), width = 6, height = 4)
g
```


# Transcripts per Gene

Now, we will plot the distribution of Ensembl Transcript IDs per Ensembl Gene ID. We will plot the distribution in our filtered expression dataset as well as the original transcripts per gene found in GENCODE (for hg19). 
```{r, echo = F}
# get transcript per gene info for own data
features <- fData(transcript_summaries)[, c("transcript_id", "gene_id")]
features <- separate_rows(features, transcript_id, gene_id, sep = "\\|")
features <- features[!duplicated(features), ]
freqs <- as.data.frame(table(as.data.frame(table(features$gene_id))$Freq))

# get transcript per gene info for Gencode (filter exactly as in the preprocessing)
genes <- gencode[gencode$type == "transcript"]
genes <- as.data.frame(genes)[, c("gene_id", "transcript_id")]
genes <- genes[!duplicated(genes), ]
freqs2 <- as.data.frame(table(as.data.frame(table(genes$gene_id))$Freq))

# get tDEGenes freq
ids <- features[features$transcript_id %in% tDEGenes$`Ensembl Transcript ID`, "gene_id"]
tfeatures <- features[features$gene_id %in% ids, ]
tfeatures <- separate_rows(tfeatures, transcript_id, gene_id, sep = "\\|")
tfeatures <- tfeatures[!duplicated(tfeatures), ]
freqs3 <- as.data.frame(table(as.data.frame(table(tfeatures$gene_id))$Freq))
freqs3$Var1 <- as.numeric(freqs3$Var1)
freqs3$Freq <- as.numeric(freqs3$Freq)
print(paste0("Number of all tDEGene transcripts: ", sum(rowSums(freqs3[, c("Var1", "Freq")]))))

# merge all three datasets
tfreq <- merge(freqs, freqs2, by = "Var1", all = T)
tfreq <- merge(tfreq, freqs3, by = "Var1", all = T)
# change colnames
colnames(tfreq) <- c("TranscriptCount", "ExpressionFreq", "OriginalFreq", "tDEGeneFreq")
# melt into ggplot format
tfreq <- reshape2::melt(tfreq, id.vars = "TranscriptCount")
tfreq$TranscriptCount <- as.numeric(tfreq$TranscriptCount)
# remove rows with NA and change factor order
tfreq <- tfreq[complete.cases(tfreq), ]
tfreq$variable <- factor(tfreq$variable, levels = c("OriginalFreq", "ExpressionFreq", "tDEGeneFreq"))

g <- ggplot(tfreq, aes(x = TranscriptCount, y = value, color = variable)) +
  geom_line(size = 1.2) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 15), legend.position = c(0.9, 0.9), legend.box.background = element_rect(colour = "black"), legend.title = element_blank(), plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) +
  ggtitle("Transcripts") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0.015, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0.01, 0)) +
  labs(x = "Number of transcripts per gene", y = "Number of genes") +
  scale_color_manual(values = viridis(3, begin = 0.3, end = 0.9, option = "D"), labels = c("GENCODE", "Own genes", "tDEGenes"))
ggsave(plot = g, file = paste0(outpath, "/2.4_plot_transcripts_per_gene_gencode_vs_own_data.pdf"))
g
# save tDEGenes transcript counts as result table
colnames(freqs3) <- c("#Transcripts", "#Genes")
freqs3$Type <- "tDEGenes"
write.table(freqs3, paste0(results_path, "/2.6_tDEGenes_transcript_counts.tsv"), sep = "\t")
rm(features, genes, freqs, freqs2, freqs3, tfreq)
```


# Exons per Gene

Now, we will plot the distribution of Ensembl Exon IDs per Ensembl Gene ID. We will plot the distribution in our filtered expression dataset as well as the original exons per gene found in GENCODE (for hg19). 
```{r, echo = F}
features <- fData(exon_summaries)[, c("exon_id", "gene_id")]
features <- separate_rows(features, exon_id, gene_id, sep = "\\|")
features <- features[!duplicated(features), ]
freqs <- as.data.frame(table(as.data.frame(table(features$gene_id))$Freq))

# load gene to transcript info from Gencode and filter exactly like in the preprocessing step
genes <- gencode[gencode$type == "exon"]
genes <- as.data.frame(genes)[, c("gene_id", "exon_id")]

# get only Ensembl gene IDs for which we have exons (see above)
genes <- genes[genes$gene_id %in% features$gene_id, ]
genes <- genes[!duplicated(genes), ]
freqs2 <- as.data.frame(table(as.data.frame(table(genes$gene_id))$Freq))

# get eDEGenes freq
ids <- features[features$exon_id %in% eDEGenes$`Ensembl Exon ID`, "gene_id"]
efeatures <- features[features$gene_id %in% ids, ]
efeatures <- separate_rows(efeatures, exon_id, gene_id, sep = "\\|")
efeatures <- efeatures[!duplicated(efeatures), ]
freqs3 <- as.data.frame(table(as.data.frame(table(efeatures$gene_id))$Freq))
freqs3$Var1 <- as.numeric(freqs3$Var1)
freqs3$Freq <- as.numeric(freqs3$Freq)
print(paste0("Number of all eDEGene exons: ", sum(rowSums(freqs3[, c("Var1", "Freq")]))))

# merge all three datasets
efreq <- merge(freqs, freqs2, by = "Var1", all = T)
efreq <- merge(efreq, freqs3, by = "Var1", all = T)
# change colnames
colnames(efreq) <- c("ExonCount", "ExpressionFreq", "OriginalFreq", "eDEGeneFreq")
# melt into ggplot format
efreq <- reshape2::melt(efreq, id.vars = "ExonCount")
efreq$ExonCount <- as.numeric(efreq$ExonCount)
# remove rows with NA and change factor order
efreq <- efreq[complete.cases(efreq), ]
efreq$variable <- factor(efreq$variable, levels = c("OriginalFreq", "ExpressionFreq", "eDEGeneFreq"))

g <- ggplot(efreq, aes(x = ExonCount, y = value, color = variable)) +
  geom_line(size = 1.2) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 15), legend.position = c(0.9, 0.9), legend.box.background = element_rect(colour = "black"), legend.title = element_blank(), plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) +
  ggtitle("Exons") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0.015, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0.01, 0)) +
  labs(x = "Number of exons per gene", y = "Number of genes") +
  scale_color_manual(values = viridis(3, begin = 0.3, end = 0.9, option = "D"), labels = c("GENCODE", "Own data", "eDEGenes"))
ggsave(plot = g, file = paste0(outpath, "/3.4_plot_exons_per_gene_gencode_vs_own_data.pdf"))
g
# save eDEGenes exon counts as result table
freqs3$variable <- as.character("eDEGenes")
colnames(freqs3) <- c("#Exons", "#Genes", "Type")
write.table(freqs3, paste0(results_path, "/3.6_eDEGenes_exon_counts.tsv"), sep = "\t")
rm(features, genes, freqs, freqs2, freqs3, tfreq)
```
